Let

\[
S=\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\sum_{j=1}^{100}2^{-\left\lfloor 101k/j\right\rfloor}.
\]

For a fixed \(j\), write each positive integer \(k\) uniquely as

\[
k=a+tj,\qquad 1\le a\le j,\quad t\ge 0.
\]

Then

\[
\left\lfloor \frac{101k}{j}\right\rfloor
=\left\lfloor \frac{101a}{j}\right\rfloor+101t.
\]

Hence

\[
\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}2^{-\lfloor 101k/j\rfloor}
=\frac{1}{1-2^{-101}}\sum_{a=1}^{j}2^{-\lfloor 101a/j\rfloor}.
\]

So

\[
S=\frac{T}{1-2^{-101}},
\]

where

\[
T=\sum_{1\le a\le j\le 100}2^{-\lfloor 101a/j\rfloor}.
\]

Now count the number \(N_m\) of pairs \((a,j)\) such that

\[
\left\lfloor \frac{101a}{j}\right\rfloor=m.
\]

Since \(1\le a/j\le 1\), we have \(m\in\{1,\dots,101\}\).

- If \(m=101\), then \(a=j\), so \(N_{101}=100\).
- If \(1\le m\le 100\), let \(r=101-m\). Then

\[
m\le \frac{101a}{j}<m+1
\]

is equivalent to

\[
\frac{r-1}{101}<\frac{j-a}{j}\le \frac{r}{101}.
\]

For each \(j\le 100\), this interval for \((j-a)/j\) has length \(1/101<1/j\), so it contributes at most one value of \(j-a\). It contributes exactly when

\[
\left\lfloor \frac{rj}{101}\right\rfloor-\left\lfloor \frac{(r-1)j}{101}\right\rfloor=1.
\]

Thus

\[
N_{101-r}=\sum_{j=1}^{100}\left(\left\lfloor \frac{rj}{101}\right\rfloor-\left\lfloor \frac{(r-1)j}{101}\right\rfloor\right).
\]

Because \(101\) is prime, for \(1\le r\le 100\),

\[
\sum_{j=1}^{100}\left\lfloor \frac{rj}{101}\right\rfloor=50(r-1).
\]

Therefore

\[
N_m=50\quad(1\le m\le 99),\qquad N_{100}=0,\qquad N_{101}=100.
\]

So

\[
\begin{aligned}
T
&=50\sum_{m=1}^{99}2^{-m}+100\cdot 2^{-101} \\
&=50(1-2^{-99})+100\cdot 2^{-101} \\
&=50(1-2^{-100}).
\end{aligned}
\]

Therefore

\[
\begin{aligned}
S
&=\frac{50(1-2^{-100})}{1-2^{-101}} \\
&=\frac{100(2^{100}-1)}{2^{101}-1}.
\end{aligned}
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{100(2^{100}-1)}{2^{101}-1}}
\]
